p01.why: B's legs have elbow and knee bulges, tapered shins and a fuller hind thigh, where A's legs are plain straight tubes.

p02.why: The ankylosaur is practically identical; B's belly sits a hair lower (92 vs 91 cm tall), with no quality difference.

p03.why: The horned beetle renders are indistinguishable in every view.

p04.why: Only tiny shifts in neck width and colour-band edges on the head; both snakes read equally well.

p05.why: In front and top views B's long arms hang free of the torso and the legs part at the crotch, while A's arms and thighs fuse into the body.

p06.why: The striped ram-horned biped is near-identical; the thigh and knee shading differs by only a few pixels.

p07.why: The small salamander only differs by fractional limb thickness; nothing to choose between them.

p08.why: The tusked boar is near-identical; the back curve and ear angle move a few pixels.

p09.why: B's thighs and upper legs are broader and taper into the knee for believable mass, where A's are thin tubes, though B shows slight pale smears at the leg roots.

p10.why: The scorpion is near-identical; only the pincer-arm root under the head shifts slightly.

p11.why: In front view A's head is clearly wider than the neck with a deeper open mouth; B's narrower head blends into an almost equally wide neck column.

p12.why: B's thighs are drumstick-shaped and taper to the knee with a clean crotch; A's inner thighs bulge into a rounded, pants-like crotch.

p13.why: The bear-like quadruped is near-identical; only the belly line between the legs sits marginally lower in B.

p14.why: In front view A's forelegs flare out into a skirt-like mass under the chest; B's forelegs drop as clean columns with a clearer elbow in side view.

p15.why: The camo salamander is near-identical; the upper-arm roundness differs only slightly.

p16.why: B's lower leg segments have a serrated, faceted outline in the side view; A's legs are smooth and tapered.

p17.why: B's thighs separate at a clear crotch notch and read as two legs; A's fuller thighs fuse together at the crotch.

p18.why: B's raised body tapers into a narrower neck under the head so the head reads as distinct; A's neck is as wide as the head and swells straight into the bulb.

p19.why: The rhino is near-identical; only the ear and shoulder-hump height shifts marginally.

p20.why: Slight trade-offs only: B's belly hangs a little lower (1.2 vs 1.3 m tall) and A's legs are a touch thicker, with no clear winner.
